notes.title: Alder & Finch / launch workspace
notes.summary: Team, project, and source map for the spring reporting release.
notes.body: Alder & Finch Commerce is a fictional multi-brand retailer. The Launch operations team prepares customer communications for the Spring reporting release. Reporting engineering verifies the production revision and test result. Every availability statement is checked against the audience actually included in the current rollout.

notes.title: Decision / CSV export audience
notes.summary: At the October 16 review, R17 access was limited to internal testers.
notes.body: At the October 16 review, the team approved internal tester access for CSV export in production revision R17. The release did not then support a claim that every account could use CSV export. A broader claim needs a new reviewed rollout record and a current passing production test. This is a dated decision; check the live campaign review for current access. Draft copy remains under human review.

notes.title: Playbook / launch evidence review
notes.summary: A short checklist for checking product claims and preparing a reviewer handover.
notes.body: 1. Identify the exact promise and named audience in each draft. 2. Confirm the running production revision and linked feature. 3. Read the current rollout audience and source, then the current test on that revision. 4. Mark unsupported or missing evidence for review. 5. Prepare an internal proposal; a person approves any draft change. If the review owner is unavailable, use a confirmed backup and this source-backed checklist.

notes.title: Campaign / spring reporting brief
notes.summary: Audience, customer benefit, and editorial opening for the launch campaign.
notes.body: Audience: Alder & Finch customer accounts. Lead with one reader benefit: weekly reporting in one clear view. Avoid a feature list as the opening. The approved tone is stored as a versioned campaign instruction and must be checked before a writer resumes an older handoff. Product availability claims must be checked separately against rollout evidence.

notes.title: Review / first email opening
notes.summary: A reviewer rejected a feature-list opening and recorded why.
notes.body: The first proposed email opened with a list of dashboards, exports, filters, and alerts. The editor rejected that opening because it did not give the reader one clear benefit. This review is a dated episode for this campaign. It is not a new company-wide writing rule.

notes.title: Handoff / planner to writer
notes.summary: The original handoff saved brief revision 1; a new writer must check current instructions.
notes.body: The planning agent prepared the launch email task under brief revision 1. It handed the task, initial tone, opening rule, and reviewed feedback to the writing agent. The handoff is a historical snapshot. A fresh writer session must compare it with approved current instructions before drafting.

notes.title: Roster review / launch evidence

notes.body: At roster revision 1, Maya Chen was confirmed as primary owner of launch evidence review. The roster was reviewed as complete and recorded no approved backup. This is a historical baseline; use the live assignment graph for current coverage after a manager approves a backup.

notes.title: Playbook / release QA sign-off
notes.summary: Engineering checks the R17 production test and reports any missing result.
notes.body: Reporting engineering confirms that revision R17 is running and the CSV export smoke test passed. Leo Brooks is the primary owner and Ines Alvarez is the reviewed backup for this demo process. Missing or stale test evidence leaves claim review uncertain; the QA process does not approve marketing copy.
